title: Attack on Titan 2
synopsis: Omega Force’s omni-directional-gear action game adapting the anime’s first two seasons — retained as the Koei Tecmo Nintendo Switch game card.

catalog.mediumForm: Nintendo Switch game card · retail edition

custody.physical: Nintendo Switch game card in retail case

curatorNotes:
Attack on Titan 2 is Omega Force’s second game based on Hajime Isayama’s manga, retelling the story through the anime’s first two seasons with an original ending. Players swing through the air on omni-directional mobility gear to bring down Titans, and the sequel adds a character creator, a co-op story mode, and a town life mode built around relationships with the cast.

Koei Tecmo released it in Japan on March 15, 2018, and in North America on March 20, 2018, with Nintendo Switch among the launch platforms.

This filing opens the Attack on Titan lineage on the shelf.
collectionNotes:
The retained object is Koei Tecmo’s retail edition of Attack on Titan 2 on a Nintendo Switch game card.

Dedicated artifact views of the individual copy have not yet been filed; the gallery below is held open for that documentation.

preservation.playableOn: Nintendo Switch; compatible Nintendo Switch family hardware
preservation.compatibility: Nintendo Switch software is region-free. The retained game card is the primary access copy and runs on any Nintendo Switch console.
preservation.concerns: Game cards are flash media; long-term charge retention, contact wear, and loss of the small card from its case are the principal risks. Any content delivered as an eShop download or update depends on Nintendo’s servers and is not preserved by the card alone.
preservation.knownRevisions: Released in Japan on March 15, 2018 (as 進撃の巨人2) and in North America on March 20, 2018; sold as A.O.T. 2 in PAL regions. The Final Battle expansion followed on July 5, 2019, both as an upgrade pack and as a separate retail edition, Attack on Titan 2: Final Battle, which is not this filing.
preservation.availability: Distributed at retail by Koei Tecmo, with a digital edition on the Nintendo eShop.
